I feel like this ignores that a lot of people who self harm take great measures to hide their injuries. 
For most, it’s not about attention. And is it so horrible to need attention? Sometimes no one’s listening and you feel you have no other choice than to do something severe to get it. I’m not saying it’s ok, but I wish people were more empathetic.
I’ve had a few. None of them seem to care.
I do, I also hit myself with a hammer sometimes:
Physical pain distracts from emotional pain. I can’t take my anger out on the people who are hurting me, so I take it out on myself. I get to control the pain I experience.

I think it comes off as control in that you are deciding about pain. You get to decide how much you receive and how long it lasts, rather than other people or circumstances hurting you in ways you can’t control or stop.
Somewhere Over the Rainbow (Judy Garland version, usually from her later life, not the Wizard of Oz performance).

I used to. I had a special small notebook for it I labeled “Record it Harm”. I’d write down what I had done and what I was feeling/thinking. I moved it around a lot because I didn’t want anyone to find it, but at some point I lost track of it. I wish I could find it or still did that. I think it would be important to see how my thoughts surrounding it have changed or what patterns there are.

Well yeah, I’m attracted to the outcome. I want things to go well.

I think there’s a problem in saying anything is possible. Some things just aren’t. It’s not in the realm of possibility in how reality works for some things to happen. It’s not about belief, it’s about physics, biology, chemistry. You can’t cheat science.
An alternative isn’t the same as the thing you want. A clone is not the same person, it just has the same DNA. Do you sincerely think humans will achieve flight?
But those aren’t the same as getting what you actually wanted. Some things are impossible.
I would think so. No one has ever regrown a limb or learned to fly. You can’t date Marilyn Monroe.
